topic.question_zh: 没有哲学背景，怎样开始认真分析伦理、死亡与日常论证？
topic.description_zh: 从具体问题和可讨论的论证进入哲学，也保留原典导读和长期哲学史路径。

resources.title: Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do?
resources.summary_zh: 通过具体道德困境讨论公正、权利与责任，介绍亚里士多德、康德、密尔和罗尔斯等思想。适合想从问题出发进入伦理与政治哲学的人。
resources.prerequisites_zh: 评论将其作为入门材料；无需先系统读完哲学史。它聚焦伦理与公正，覆盖范围并非全部哲学。
resources.why_recommended_zh: 多名评论者独立推荐，理由集中在课堂讨论引人入胜、不同公正理论讲解清晰，而非只因为哈佛品牌。

evidence.resource_title: Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do?
evidence.quote: great course on moral reasoning, covers different theories of justice based on ideas from Aristotle, Kant, John Stuart Mill, John Rawls and many more, extremely well presented too.
evidence.reason_zh: 指出课程具体涵盖的伦理理论，并肯定呈现方式。
evidence.author: ljiljana

evidence.resource_title: Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do?
evidence.quote: I saw this years ago and I am still so impressed by how engaging these lectures are. Michael Sandel is great. Of course this is not holistic review of philosophy
evidence.reason_zh: 另一讨论中的学习者肯定吸引力，并限定它不是哲学全景课程。
evidence.author: patrykp

evidence.resource_title: Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do?
evidence.quote: The Harvard Justice series (Michael Sandel) is one of the best ones I've seen. Very intriguing!
evidence.reason_zh: 2023年讲座推荐帖再次出现独立正面推荐。
evidence.author: piyush_soni

resources.notes_zh: 评论同时给出Harvard页面、YouTube系列和旧edX版；它们属于同一教学主题的不同入口，作业与认证安排可能不同。

resources.title: Think Again: How to Reason and Argue
resources.provider: Duke University / Ram Neta、Walter Sinnott-Armstrong / Coursera
resources.summary_zh: 训练识别、理解和评估论证，作为哲学推理与日常争论的基础。适合希望超越凭直觉辩论、建立明确推理步骤的人。
resources.prerequisites_zh: 评论未给出正式先修；链接指向 Understanding Arguments，不能据此声称一个入口囊括系列全部内容。
resources.why_recommended_zh: 一位评论者认为其论证基础内容广且出色；另一位有多门MOOC经验的学习者也把它列为喜欢的非技术课程。

evidence.resource_title: Think Again: How to Reason and Argue
evidence.quote: the Coursera course Think Again: How to Reason and Argue , by Duke University's Ram Neta and Walter Sinnott-Armstrong [1] is exceptional.
evidence.reason_zh: 明确命名授课者并给出强烈正面评价。
evidence.author: rikkhill

evidence.resource_title: Think Again: How to Reason and Argue
evidence.quote: For non-IT related courses I liked Think Again: How to Reason and Argue[8], Crafting an Effective Writer: Tools of the Trade (Fundamental English Writing)[9]
evidence.reason_zh: 另一位多课程学习者也明确表示喜欢Think Again；不把其完成总数等同于本课完成证明。
evidence.author: uulbiy

resources.notes_zh: 旧课程名与现有子课入口可能不同；推荐依据保留历史原名。

resources.title: Buddhism and Modern Psychology
resources.summary_zh: 把佛教中关于情绪、冥想和自我的观点与进化心理学及认知科学研究联系起来。适合对哲学与心理学交叉问题感兴趣的人。
resources.prerequisites_zh: 评论未提正式先修。推荐主要针对心理学解释和实践讨论，不是佛教宗教学全景。
resources.why_recommended_zh: 不同年份的学习者都认为它拓展了理解幸福、意义及情绪的方式；推荐理由包括理论联系和可继续阅读的材料。

evidence.quote: It includes interesting interviews and solid book/article recommendations. It's very eye-opening to me and gave me a whole new perspective about happiness and meaning in life.
evidence.reason_zh: 亲身体验肯定访谈、延伸书目和对幸福及意义的启发。
evidence.author: tianyicui

evidence.quote: This course was just mind-blowing for me. It talks a lot about how our evolutionary survival mechanisms prevent us from seeing the world clearly.
evidence.reason_zh: 另一位学习者肯定进化心理学切入的启发。
evidence.author: blocked_again

evidence.quote: Note that religious aspects are not addressed. Practical aspects of buddhism (such as a regular meditation practice, approach to emotions, etc) are discussed. I find it very useful in day to day life.
evidence.reason_zh: 给出日常应用体验，并限制推荐范围为实践而非宗教内容。
evidence.author: tra3

resources.notes_zh: 评论者赞同课程中对佛教与科学关系的解释，不能据此把课程中的所有论点视为科学定论。 本次原Coursera入口跳转至心理学分类目录，尚未确认原课程的有效现行学习入口。

link_check.content_note_zh: 原课程地址跳转至分类目录，未确认课程当前入口。

resources.title: Death (PHIL 176)
resources.summary_zh: 讨论灵魂与肉体、人格延续、死亡是否有害、不朽是否值得，以及死亡意识如何影响生活。适合愿意用论证检验人生直觉的哲学入门者。
resources.prerequisites_zh: 官网课程材料包含柏拉图、John Perry、托尔斯泰等阅读；需要愿意持续阅读和思考抽象论证。
resources.why_recommended_zh: 2023年的推荐者明确报告反复观看、完整听过且仍然喜欢；2018年另有不同作者的强烈推荐。

evidence.quote: The one I've enjoyed watching more than once: Death with Shelly Kagan, Yale
evidence.reason_zh: 明确说反复观看并喜欢。
evidence.author: dusted

evidence.quote: I don't know why, I've listened it through more than once and enjoyed it a lot.
evidence.reason_zh: 同一推荐者在另一征集帖明确报告不止一次完整听完；不重复计算为独立作者。
evidence.author: dusted

evidence.quote: Professor Kagan's class on Death from Yale is absolutely fantastic and should be general class taught imho.
evidence.author: jadbox

resources.notes_zh: 官网存档为2007年春季课堂。课程会讨论自杀的哲学与伦理问题；这是内容范围说明。

resources.title: The Philosopher's Toolkit: How to Be the Most Rational Person in Any Room
resources.format_detail_zh: 系统讲座 / 有声课程
resources.summary_zh: 介绍判断论证、选择启发式方法和解决问题的思考工具。适合希望训练日常推理、偏好长篇音频学习的人。
resources.prerequisites_zh: 评论未提正式先修；音频版由视频课程改编，可能无法完整传达视觉材料。
resources.why_recommended_zh: 推荐者认为它把各个思考工具背后的概念解释清楚，同时明确提醒音频与视频版的差别。

evidence.resource_title: The Philosopher's Toolkit: How to Be the Most Rational Person in Any Room
evidence.quote: It teaches you mental models on how to think and find a solution to a problem. It explains the concepts behind each model quite well. Topics include how to determine a valid argument, an iron clad argument, using heuristics to solve problems, among other things.
evidence.reason_zh: 给出明确推荐以及论证和启发式问题求解的具体内容。
evidence.author: accidentalrebel

resources.notes_zh: 回复者提供视频版链接；来源没有证明当前订阅、购买或图书馆借阅条件。

resources.title: Reason and Persuasion
resources.format_detail_zh: 柏拉图哲学导读教材 / Coursera讲座系列
resources.summary_zh: 从柏拉图进入哲学论证，提供教材与相应讲座。适合希望读哲学原典，又需要有结构的入门解释的人。
resources.prerequisites_zh: 评论定位为可亲近而不浅薄的入门；需要实际阅读、思考论证。
resources.why_recommended_zh: 哲学专题帖中直接推荐其作为有深度的入门路径，且给出书与课程的配套入口。来源未声称推荐者已经完整修完。

evidence.quote: For an approachable but not shallow introduction to philosophy via Plato, try Holbo and Waring's Reason and Persuasion, available as a free book and Coursera lecture series:
evidence.reason_zh: 针对柏拉图入门的明确正面推荐；不冒充完成者体验。
evidence.author: aWidebrant

resources.notes_zh: 免费是2020年评论中的表述。原www入口本次TLS证书域名不匹配，保留原始推荐链接并记录访问限制。

resources.title: History of Philosophy Without Any Gaps
resources.format_detail_zh: 连续哲学史播客 / 讲座系列
resources.summary_zh: 按历史脉络讲解哲学思想的发展，并联系科学、政治、宗教与社会环境。适合愿意长期听讲、希望补足哲学史背景的人。
resources.prerequisites_zh: 来源没有列学科先修；系列持续扩展，适合按阶段学习而非期待短期速成。
resources.why_recommended_zh: 推荐者认为它兼顾简洁与必要深度，历史背景解释出色，而且持续保持信息量与趣味性。

evidence.resource_title: History of Philosophy Without Any Gaps
evidence.quote: Peter Adamson does a fantastic job explaining the historical context and progression of philosophy along with the interplay between philosophy, science, politics, religion, and society. I find the episodes consistently both informative and amusing.
evidence.reason_zh: 对历史背景、跨领域联系及持续听讲体验的具体正面评价。
evidence.author: Fezzik

resources.notes_zh: 这是播客式系统学习资源，不能等同于有作业、批改与学分的大学MOOC；官网本次取得200页面。

link_check.page_title: Home | History of Philosophy without any gaps
